page: Amazon Web Services r8i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The instance provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It features a large 480 MB L3 cache. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1890.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.41 GB/sec. Text processing performance is in the top tier at 2742.0. Conversely, multi-core scaling is limited, as evidenced by a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 4363.0 and a weak stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 4286.46. Memory bandwidth tests also indicate weak performance for both small cached blocks (316.43 GB/sec) and larger uncached blocks (31.47 GB/sec read, 17.95 GB/sec write).

This instance offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring significant RAM without high multi-core CPU demands. It is appropriate for memory-intensive tasks such as in-memory caching, with Redis SET operations averaging 7.49 million operations per second, static web serving, text processing, and moderate database operations.
